description: Flight Booking Digital Operations Command Center. Grafana migration of the Power BI Single Pane of Glass wireframe, persona-separated into Leadership rows (executive summary, business impact, live status) and SRE rows (golden signals, dependencies, runtime, logs & traces). Read the 'Wireframe Coverage Notes' text panel at the bottom before presenting: several Power BI panels depend on ServiceNow/CMDB sources that do not exist in this stack and were intentionally omitted.

panels.title: LEADERSHIP  ·  Executive Summary
panels.description: Maps to Power BI wireframe page L1 (Executive & Governance). Decision supported: is the estate healthy enough to leave alone this hour?

panels.title: IT Health Score
panels.description: Composite: 40% availability + 30% Apdex + 30% booking success. Defined once in prometheus/recording_rules.yml (spog:it_health_score). Weights are provisional -- agree them with service owners before this goes in front of leadership.

panels.title: Availability (5m)
panels.description: 1 - (5xx rate / total rate), averaged across the selected services. SLO target 99.5%.

panels.title: Booking Success Rate (5m)
panels.description: Confirmed bookings over all booking attempts. Raw PromQL rather than the biz:booking_success:ratio5m recording rule so the $route and $payment_method variables still filter it.

panels.title: Search → Book Conversion
panels.description: Funnel conversion from search to confirmed booking. A drop here with availability still green points at a business or UX problem, not an outage.

panels.title: Worst P95 Latency
panels.description: Slowest service P95 across the selection -- deliberately max() not avg(), so one degraded service cannot be averaged out of view.

panels.title: Revenue at Risk (₹/hr)
panels.description: Annualised-to-hourly INR value of booking attempts that failed. Sourced from booking_value_at_risk_inr_total, incremented with the attempted amount on every failed booking.

panels.title: LEADERSHIP  ·  Business Service Health & Impact
panels.description: Maps to wireframe panels 'Business service health & coverage', 'Value delivered' and 'Business KPI & transaction impact'.

panels.title: Business Service Health — RAG over time
panels.description: Grafana equivalent of the wireframe RAG heatmap, with time added. Green ≥99.5%, amber ≥99%, red below, grey = no telemetry.

panels.title: Booking Funnel (5m rate)
panels.description: Drop-off between the three stages is the conversion-loss story. Stage 1 is not filtered by $payment_method because payment method is not known at search time.

panels.title: Revenue vs Revenue at Risk (₹/min)
panels.description: Business-value view of reliability. Widening red band = failures are landing on high-value bookings.

panels.title: Business KPI & Transaction Impact
panels.description: Wireframe 'Business KPI & transaction impact' table. Rows are named by each query's legendFormat, then collapsed with a reduce/lastNotNull transformation -- the standard Grafana pattern for a KPI list.

panels.title: Booking Outcome Mix (selected range)
panels.description: Confirmed versus each canonical failure reason. Failure reasons are whitelisted in the app so this legend can never explode.

panels.title: Top Routes by Confirmed Bookings
panels.description: topk(5) keeps this readable as the route catalogue grows.

panels.title: LEADERSHIP  ·  Live Operations Status
panels.description: Maps to wireframe page L3. Decision supported: is anything down right now, and is it already being handled?

panels.title: Services Up
panels.description: Scrape health. A target that stops responding shows here before any application metric can tell you.

panels.title: Targets Down
panels.description: `or vector(0)` keeps the panel green instead of showing NO DATA when nothing is down -- count() over an empty set returns no series.

panels.title: Active Chaos Simulations
panels.description: Guards against misreading an intentional experiment as a real incident. Query B names the active scenario(s).

panels.title: Estate Error Rate (5m)
panels.description: 5xx share of all requests across the selected services.

panels.title: ERROR Logs (5m)
panels.description: Loki-sourced. `| __error__=""` drops non-JSON lines from sidecar containers so the count is not inflated by parse failures.

panels.title: Payment Gateway
panels.description: Single most important dependency for revenue. min() so any unhealthy gateway shows as DOWN.

panels.title: Live Service Status
panels.description: One row per service, five instant queries joined on service_name. This is the Grafana analogue of the wireframe's leadership status table.

panels.title: Critical Error Stream (trace-correlated)
panels.description: WARNING and ERROR only, reformatted for scanning. Every line carries trace_id -- click a line, then follow the trace_id derived field into Jaeger for the full request waterfall.

panels.title: SRE  ·  Golden Signals (Traffic · Latency · Errors · Saturation)
panels.description: Maps to wireframe page S1. Decision supported: what is degrading, and how much error budget is left to spend on it?

panels.title: Traffic — requests/sec by service
panels.description: RED: Rate. $rate_window controls the smoothing window; widen it on long time ranges to avoid sawtooth artefacts.

panels.title: Latency — P50 / P95 / P99
panels.description: RED: Duration. Quantiles are computed after summing buckets by le -- never average a pre-computed quantile across services.

panels.title: Errors — 5xx/sec and error ratio
panels.description: RED: Errors. Absolute rate on the left axis, ratio on the right -- a low ratio at high traffic is a very different page than the reverse.

targets.expr: sum by (service_name) (rate(http_requests_total{environment="$environment", service_name=~"$service", status=~"5.."}[$rate_window])) / clamp_min(sum by (service_name) (rate(http_requests_total{environment="$environment", service_name=~"$service"}[$rate_window])), 0.001)

panels.title: Apdex (T = 0.25s)
panels.description: (satisfied + tolerating/2) / total, with T=0.25s and 4T=1.0s. Both are exact histogram bucket boundaries, so no interpolation error.

panels.title: Error Budget Remaining (30d)
panels.description: Against a 99.5% availability SLO over 30 days. min() shows the worst-off service -- the one that will force a freeze first.

panels.title: Error Budget Burn Rate (1h window)
panels.description: Burn rate 1× exhausts the budget exactly at 30 days. 14.4× is the standard multi-window fast-burn paging threshold (2% of a 30-day budget in 1 hour).

panels.title: SRE  ·  Payment Gateway & Dependency Health
panels.description: Maps to the wireframe's dependency / service-map panel. Decision supported: is the fault ours or the downstream gateway's?

panels.title: Payment Gateway P95 Latency by Method
panels.description: Per-method P95 against the 2s SLO. The latency chaos scenario shows here first, 3-5s injected per payment.

panels.title: Payment Gateway Latency Distribution
panels.description: Native histogram heatmap -- exposes bimodality that a P95 line hides. Two bands = two code paths or a partially degraded gateway pool.

panels.title: Payment Decline Reasons
panels.description: Business declines (insufficient_funds) versus technical failures (gateway_timeout) need completely different responses.

panels.title: Payment Success Rate by Method
panels.description: One method collapsing while others hold is an instrument-specific gateway problem, not an outage.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (payment_method) (rate(payment_transactions_total{environment="$environment", payment_method=~"$payment_method", status="success"}[$rate_window])) / clamp_min(sum by (payment_method) (rate(payment_transactions_total{environment="$environment", payment_method=~"$payment_method"}[$rate_window])), 0.001)

panels.title: Dependency Health
panels.description: booking → payment edge health. downstream_dependency_up is set by the booking service from the outcome of its last outbound call, so it reflects the caller's real experience rather than a synthetic probe.

panels.title: Payments In Flight (saturation)
panels.description: USE: Saturation. Concurrency climbing while throughput is flat means requests are queueing -- the leading indicator of a latency incident.

panels.title: SRE  ·  Runtime & Resource Saturation
panels.description: Sourced from the process_* / python_* metrics prometheus_client exposes automatically. No node_exporter or cAdvisor is deployed in this stack -- see the coverage note at the bottom of the dashboard.

panels.title: Resident Memory by Service
panels.description: Red at 300MB matches the FlightSearchHighMemory alert threshold in alert_rules.yml, so the panel and the alert cannot drift apart.

panels.title: Resident Memory Trend — memory-leak chaos detector
panels.description: A monotonic staircase here is the leak. Query B overlays chaos state scaled to the axis, so an intentional experiment is visually distinguishable from a genuine regression.

panels.title: CPU Utilisation by Service
panels.description: Percent of one CPU core. Values above 100 mean multiple cores are busy.

panels.title: Seats Available by Flight
panels.description: Inventory saturation. Zero seats produces booking failures with reason=no_seats, which is expected business behaviour and must not be escalated as a reliability incident.

panels.title: Open File Descriptors
panels.description: Descriptor exhaustion presents as connection errors that look like a network fault. Plotted against the actual rlimit.

panels.title: SRE  ·  Logs, Traces & Error Analysis
panels.description: Loki and Jaeger. Decision supported: what exactly failed, and on which request?

panels.title: Log Volume by Level
panels.description: Stacked log volume. A sudden ERROR band is often visible before a metric-based alert fires, because logs are not bucketed.

panels.title: Top Error Sources
panels.description: Pareto of error messages -- the wireframe's 'recurring incident Pareto', built from logs. Caution: `message` is high-cardinality. If this panel gets slow, add `| pattern` to normalise messages into templates before grouping.

panels.title: Live Log Tail — full stream
panels.description: Full structured stream for the current selection. Enable Live tailing from the panel menu for real-time follow. trace_id and span_id are extracted by | json and become clickable derived fields into Jaeger.

options.content:
### Getting from a symptom to a trace

1. Narrow the time range on **Errors — 5xx/sec** or **Log Volume by Level**.
2. Open **Live Log Tail**, expand an `ERROR` line, and click the `trace_id`
   derived field. Grafana opens the correlated Jaeger trace.
3. In Jaeger, the `call-payment-service` span shows whether the time was spent
   in booking or in the downstream gateway.

The `trace_id` derived field is configured in `datasources.yaml` on the Loki
datasource. If clicking does nothing, confirm the Jaeger datasource UID there
still matches.

---

### Wireframe panels that this stack cannot source — read before the demo

The Power BI wireframe was built for an estate fed by ServiceNow ITSM/ITOM,
Dynatrace, Moogsoft and a CACI maturity scorecard. Several of its panels have
**no equivalent telemetry** in Prometheus, Loki or Jaeger, and were deliberately
left out rather than faked:

| Wireframe panel | Required source | Status here |
|---|---|---|
| MTTR / MTTD / MTTA by LOB | ServiceNow incident timestamps | **Not available** — no ticketing system deployed |
| SLA compliance % and breach-by-group | ServiceNow SLA records | **Not available** |
| Monitoring coverage % (62% target 90%) | CMDB app inventory vs monitored apps | **Not available** — needs a CMDB to divide by |
| Automated / machine-assisted resolution % | Automation platform (UiPath, Resolve) | **Not available** |
| Neuro maturity scorecard, 5 dimensions | CACI KPI workbook, scored manually | **Not available** — monthly manual assessment, not telemetry |
| Governance & audit findings | ServiceNow GRC | **Not available** |
| Incident / change / CI correlation | ServiceNow CMDB + ITSM | **Not available** |
| LOB dimension on every panel | CMDB business-service mapping | **Partially modelled** — `business_service` and `tier` target labels in `prometheus.yml` are the hook; populate them properly when a CMDB exists |

**What replaced them.** Every panel above is an *organisational* measure —
how fast humans respond, how much of the estate is instrumented, how mature the
practice is. Grafana's strength is the *technical* measure: what the system is
doing this second. So the Leadership rows here answer the same executive
questions (is it healthy, is value at risk, is it handled) using live signals
instead of ticket derivatives: **Availability** and **Apdex** in place of SLA
compliance, **Revenue at Risk ₹/hr** in place of business-impact ratings,
**Error Budget Remaining** in place of a maturity score.

**Recommended split.** Keep Power BI as the system of record for the
ServiceNow-derived and manually-scored KPIs on a daily-to-monthly cadence. Use
this Grafana dashboard for everything real-time. Wire them together with a Power
BI tile that links to this dashboard and a Grafana text panel linking back —
do not try to reproduce ServiceNow KPIs in Grafana from Prometheus, because
there is no honest way to compute them here.

**If you do want MTTR in Grafana**, the smallest credible path is a ServiceNow
→ Prometheus exporter (or an Infinity datasource querying the ServiceNow Table
API directly). That is a separate piece of work and should be scoped as one.

list.name: environment
list.label: Environment
list.description: Populated from the `environment` target label in prometheus.yml.

list.name: service
list.label: Service
list.description: allValue is an explicit service regex, not `.*`. The same variable feeds Loki stream selectors, and `.*` there would pull in grafana/prometheus/promtail container logs.

list.name: route
list.label: Flight Route
list.description: Route values are whitelisted in the app, so this list stays short.

list.name: log_level
list.label: Log Level
list.description: Defaults to WARNING+ERROR so the log panels open on signal, not noise.

list.name: rate_window
list.label: Rate Window
list.description: Smoothing window for rate() in the SRE rows. Leadership rows use fixed-5m recording rules on purpose so exec KPIs do not move when someone changes this.
